conviction_note: Near non-result. The findings sum to +0.9 (crowded short, a possible term-debt fix for the $1.0B 2027 convert, and a quarter whose bar sits in the lower half of the company's own guide) against small negatives (new CFO's first print, a possible BetterHelp goodwill charge). The scaled number is slightly negative at p_up 49 x abs 12 because the print turns on the BetterHelp cash-pay guide, which I could not read from any independent series. The +11.3 put skew says downside is paid for, and the last guide cut took the stock down 28%. The two measurements disagree in sign and both are small.

positioning_check: Short interest is 32.07M shares, 17.78% of float, 8.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-10-15. That is up 6.5% from 30.10M on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/TDOC/short-interest/), so the short is crowded and was still building into the print. The baseline skew of +11.3 vol points means downside is paid for; put/call OI is 0.7. Run-up is +14.7% over 20 days and +5.6% over 5 days: the stock is at $6.655 against $5.65 on 2026-10-02 (CAO Form 4) and $6.24 on 2026-10-26. findings.finding: The reported-quarter bar is soft. Street revenue consensus is ~$585.6M (Earnings Whispers), below the $589M midpoint of the company's own $569-609M Q3 guide. In Q2, revenue of $606.9M beat consensus. The beat is likely, but it lands inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-29 Q2 beat consensus on revenue and the stock fell 28.3% on the BetterHelp guide cut, so this name does not pay for the reported line when the guide moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the consensus is visibly anchored inside the guide. If the market had priced a clean beat, the 20d run-up would come with a narrowing skew. Instead skew is +11.3, so the market cares about the guide, not this line.
findings.independence: Consensus from https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/tdoc. This shares the guide document with the BetterHelp insurance finding.

findings.finding: Phase one of the 2027 convert plan may land now. The $1.0B 1.25% notes mature 2027-06-01, have a conversion date of 2026-12-01 and have sat in current liabilities since Q2. On the Q1 call management said it would pay down a large part with cash and add new term debt 'potentially before year-end'. No refinancing 8-K had been filed by 2026-10-28 (the last 8-Ks are 5.02 items), so an announcement with or alongside Q3 would remove the overhang.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a refinancing for this name in the baseline window. The Q2 call answered no debt questions and the stock fell 28% on the operating guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The timing is unannounced, and the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001477449/000147744926000038/tdoc-20260630.htm) describes no transaction. If the market had priced the fix, the debt-overhang short (17.8% of float, rising) would be shrinking, not growing. What the money buys: repaying the convert out of ~$774M cash plus term debt cuts gross leverage (3.6x gross, 0.8x net), so it is not distress funding. Asked as a question, it comes out a small positive or zero.
findings.independence: The 10-Q Q2 2026 liquidity text is a different document and confirms the notes are current, with a $297M undrawn revolver and no transaction yet. Both are company documents.

findings.finding: A BetterHelp goodwill impairment is possible in Q3. All $283.2M of goodwill sits in BetterHelp. Q2 was already a triggering event, and fair value exceeded carrying value but no headroom was disclosed. The 10-Q says a sustained share-price decline could cause an impairment. The stock fell from ~$9.5 (late July) to ~$5.65 (early October) during the quarter. Market cap at $6.655 is ~$1.2B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A $59.1M goodwill impairment in H1 2025 coincided with the 2025-02-26 print (-13.6%), but that move was driven by guidance. Non-cash and below operating income.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is unquantified and the consensus EPS of -$0.23 does not include it. Being non-cash, it would mainly hit GAAP EPS headlines. It is sized small because it has no path to the guide or to adjusted EBITDA.
findings.independence: This is an inference from the quarter's price path. No other source quantifies it.

findings.finding: The short is crowded: 32.07M shares, 17.78% of float, 8.2 days to cover on 2026-10-15, up 6.5% from 2026-09-30. It is still building into a print whose bar sits inside the guide, so the squeeze is a mechanism on any guide that holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-02-25 the stock rose +15.1% and on 2025-10-23/29 +10% and +6.2% on prints where the guide held. Short interest was 13-18% of float in 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +14.7% 20d run-up may already include covering. But short interest rose into mid-October, so the run-up was not mainly a squeeze. If it were, settled short interest would be falling.
findings.independence: The baseline's +11.3 skew points the other way (downside paid). That is the counterweight, which is why this finding is not sized larger.

findings.finding: New CFO Michael Grasher (appointed 2026-08-31, from P&C insurer IFG) gives his first earnings call on this print. CLO Adam Vandervoort is resigning effective 2026-11-01 'with good reason' under his severance agreement (8-K 2026-09-25), and director David Snow retired 2026-09-30. That raises the odds of a conservative 2027 framing or a reset of the BetterHelp outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guide change (2026-07-29, BetterHelp cut) cost -28.3%. In 2025-02-26 the FY guide cost -13.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because the skew already pays for downside. It is filed small because nothing in the documents says the guide will move. 'Good reason' means a material change in role or conditions, which is unusual wording for a routine departure. If the market had priced a reset, the run-up would not be +14.7%.
findings.independence: The CFO appointment is in a separate document (https://www.teladochealth.com/newsroom/press/teladoc-health-appoints-michael-grasher-as-chief-financial-officer). On the Q2 call management declined to say whether cash-pay trends stabilised in July (https://www.webull.com/news/15364540438504448).

findings.finding: Arithmetic on the BetterHelp insurance ramp. The company said over 20,000 insurance sessions were completed in the final week of Q2, and Q2 insurance revenue was $21.8M. Holding that weekly rate flat through Q3 already gives roughly the $25-31M Q3 insurance guide if revenue per session is ~$100. Any growth puts insurance at or above the top of the guide. The FY $90-105M insurance range was reaffirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 insurance grew to $21.8M from $2.1M, but the stock fell 28% on the cash-pay decline. Insurance has not driven the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue per session is not disclosed, so this is an inference. It also lands inside the guide. Cash pay (~85% of the segment) is what moves the stock, and I found no independent series for it, so this is sized near zero.
findings.independence: This shares the Q2 call with the bar and the CFO findings. ChoosingTherapy (https://www.choosingtherapy.com/?p=107244, updated 2026-10-21) confirms 50-state coverage but provider availability still limited. Net of the rest: Integrated Care (~65% of revenue) is guided flat to +3%.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive (crowded and still-rising short, soft bar, possible debt fix), which cuts against the +11.3 put skew. The +14.7% 20d run-up removes some of the squeeze fuel. So p_up is held near 50, and the scaled number is slightly negative while the findings sum is slightly positive.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the reported-quarter bar finding cut from +0.5 to +0.2 and print_vs_bar from +0.8 to +0.5, because consensus sits inside the company's Q3 range.
Rule 5 (proxy/inference): the insurance-session arithmetic cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because revenue per session is undisclosed and the finding lands inside the guide.
Rule 7 (negative agreeing with the skew is priced; crowded short shrinks negatives): the management-turnover guide-risk finding cut from -0.8 to -0.5.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the convert/term-debt finding kept at +0.5 after asking what the money buys (repaying the 2027 convert, lower gross debt, not distress).

Rule 2 (one-offs): the goodwill impairment left at -0.3. It is non-cash with no path to the guide; refiled under reported_quarter per the impairment exception but kept small because it is an inference.
Lessons on pessimism artefact and crowded short: p_up moved from 48 to 49; abs_move_pct left at 12.
